definition_en: to move faster, or to make something happen sooner
core_image: 一辆车驶出弯道，猛踩油门，尾灯拉成一条线
scene: 车队驶出弯道，车手猛踩油门，速度一下子提了上去。The car accelerated smoothly onto the highway.
sceneCN: 这里的 accelerate 指「加速」（第 1 个义项：使运动速度变快）；句意是汽车平稳加速驶上高速。

senses.title: To move faster
senses.definition: moves or travels at increasing speed
senses.definitionCN: 以越来越快的速度移动或行驶
senses.example: The train accelerated as it left the station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车离站时加快了速度。
senses.why: The Latin root celer means swift, so the first sense is simply a vehicle gaining speed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 celer 意为迅捷，第一个义项就是交通工具把速度提上去。

senses.title: To quicken a process
senses.definition: makes a process happen more quickly
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程发生得更快
senses.example: The new software accelerated the work.
senses.exampleCN: 新软件加快了工作进度。
senses.why: A process can gain speed the way a car does, so the verb moves from the road to daily work.
senses.whyCN: 过程能像车一样提速，动词于是从路面走到了日常工作。

senses.title: To bring forward
senses.definition: moves an event to an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 把某个事件移到更早的时间
senses.example: They accelerated the launch by a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把发布提前了一个月。
senses.why: Making a date come sooner is speeding up the calendar rather than a body.
senses.whyCN: 让日期早点到来，加速的是日历，而不是物体。

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix meaning towards with a root meaning swift.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示「朝向」的拉丁前缀与意为「迅捷」的词根接在一起。

items.en: celer meant swift, as in a fast horse.
items.cn: celer 意为迅捷，如快马一般。

items.en: celeritas named speed itself.
items.cn: celeritas 指速度本身。

items.en: accelerare meant to hasten something.
items.cn: accelerare 意为催促、加快某事。

items.en: accelerate entered English as a verb of hastening.
items.cn: accelerate 进入英语时是表示「催促」的动词。

items.en: it now covers cars, growth, learning and disease.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖车辆、增长、学习与疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group is the acceleration family; the near-meaning group is other verbs of hurrying.
note.cn: 形近组是 acceleration 词族；近义组是别的表示催促的词。

entries.definition: a pedal or machine that speeds things up
to make a process run faster

normalIntro.en: These hints follow celer, the Latin word for swift.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语里表示「迅捷」的 celer。

normal.en: celer is Latin for swift, the heart of the word.
normal.cn: celer 是拉丁语的「迅捷」，正是词的核心。

normal.en: ad- means towards, so accelerate is to move towards speed.
normal.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「朝向」，accelerate 就是朝速度去。

normal.en: -ate makes a verb out of the Latin stem.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词干变成动词。

abstract.cn: 想象速度表的指针猛地扫向右边。

abstract.en: Picture a runner bursting off the starting line.
abstract.cn: 想象短跑者冲出起跑线。

abstract.en: Think of calendar pages flipping faster and faster.
abstract.cn: 想象日历的纸页越翻越快。

examples.cn: 汽车平稳加速驶上高速。

examples.en: New laws may accelerate the pace of change.
examples.cn: 新法律可能加快变革的步伐。

examples.en: Warm weather accelerates the growth of plants.
examples.cn: 温暖的天气加快植物生长。

definition_zh: 口音；重音；重音符号；强调
definition_en: the way a group speaks, a stressed syllable, or special emphasis
core_image: 一句话说到某个音节时，声音轻轻往上一挑
scene: 她一张口，尾音轻轻上扬，听得出不是本地人。His accent told us he had grown up abroad.
sceneCN: 这里的 accent 指「口音」（第 1 个义项：说话带出的地方语音特征）；句意是他的口音表明他在国外长大。

pos.zh: 口音；重音；重音符号；强调

derivatives.zh: 义为「重音的；按重音节拍的」

senses.title: A way of speaking
senses.definition: the way a group or region pronounces a language
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体或地区说话发音的方式
senses.example: His accent told us he had grown up abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他的口音表明他在国外长大。
senses.why: The Latin root cantus means song, and accent first named the tune of the voice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 cantus 意为歌唱，accent 最初指嗓音的调子。

senses.title: A stressed syllable
senses.definition: the stronger beat given to one syllable in a word
senses.definitionCN: 一个词中某个音节读得更强
senses.example: The accent falls on the second syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 重音落在第二个音节上。
senses.why: A raised beat in speech is a small song inside a word.
senses.whyCN: 说话时抬高的那一拍，是词里的一小段歌。

senses.title: A written mark
senses.definition: a mark placed over a letter to show its sound
senses.definitionCN: 写在字母上方以标示读音的符号
senses.example: The word carries an accent on the final e.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词最后一个 e 上带一个符号。
senses.why: The tune of the voice was written down as a small mark.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音的调子被写下来，就成了一个小符号。

senses.title: Special emphasis
senses.definition: special importance given to an idea or detail
senses.definitionCN: 给予某个想法或细节的特别重视
senses.example: The report puts the accent on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把重点放在安全上。
senses.why: A stressed beat in speech became a stressed point in argument.
senses.whyCN: 言语中加重的一拍，成了论述里被加重的一点。

senses.title: To stress a word
senses.definition: to pronounce a syllable or word more strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把某个音节或词读得更重
senses.example: Accent the first syllable in this name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名字的第一个音节要重读。
senses.why: The verb simply performs the stress that the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词做的，正是名词所指的那一下加重。

intro.en: The word goes back to a Latin noun for song added to speech.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到表示「加在言语上的歌」的拉丁名词。

items.en: cantus meant singing or a song.
items.cn: cantus 意为歌唱、歌曲。

items.en: accentus meant a tone added to speech.
items.cn: accentus 指加在言语上的调子。

items.en: accent carried the musical sense into French.
items.cn: accent 把这个音乐性的意义带进法语。

items.en: accent entered English for the tune of the voice.

items.en: it now covers regional speech, stress and written marks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖地方口音、重音与书写符号。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accent family; the near-meaning group is other words about speech sound.
note.cn: 形近组是 accent 词族；近义组是别的与语音有关的词。

abstract.en: Think of a finger tapping one beat harder.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在某一拍上敲得更重。

definition_en: to take what is offered, agree to it, or admit it as true
core_image: 一双手伸出去，把递来的东西接住
scene: 她伸手接过那封信，什么也没说。She accepted the letter without a word.
sceneCN: 这里的 accept 指「接受」（第 1 个义项：把别人递来的东西收下）；句意是她一言不发地收下了那封信。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ance 构成，义为「接受；认可」

senses.title: To take what is offered
senses.definition: takes something that someone offers or gives
senses.definitionCN: 把别人给出或递来的东西收下
senses.example: She accepted the letter without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她一言不发地收下了那封信。
senses.why: The Latin root capere means to take, and accepting is taking what is held out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 capere 意为拿取，accept 就是接过别人递来的东西。

senses.title: To agree to
senses.definition: agrees to an offer, plan or invitation
senses.definitionCN: 对提议、计划或邀请表示同意
senses.example: He accepted the job on the spot.
senses.exampleCN: 他当场接受了这份工作。
senses.why: Taking a proposal is making it your own, which is agreement.
senses.whyCN: 把提议接过来当成自己的，就是同意。

senses.title: To admit as true
senses.definition: admits that something is true or correct
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事是真实或正确的
senses.example: Most scientists accept the theory.
senses.exampleCN: 多数科学家接受这一理论。
senses.why: An idea taken into the mind as true is accepted in the same way as an object in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 被心里当成真的收下的观念，与手里接住的物件是同一个动作。

senses.title: To bear without protest
senses.definition: endures something unpleasant without resisting
senses.definitionCN: 不抗拒地承受不快之事
senses.example: She accepted the loss with great calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常平静地承受了这次失去。
senses.why: What cannot be refused is still taken in, and the verb covers that quiet bearing.
senses.whyCN: 无法拒绝的东西仍被接住，动词便涵盖这种安静的承受。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning to take to oneself.
intro.cn: 这个词出自意为「接到自己这边」的拉丁动词。

items.en: capere meant to take or seize.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取、抓住。

items.en: accipere meant to receive, formed with ad-.
items.cn: accipere 意为接收，由前缀 ad- 构成。

items.en: acceptare meant to keep receiving.
items.cn: acceptare 意为反复地接收。

items.en: accepter carried the sense into French.
items.cn: accepter 把这一意义带进法语。

items.en: accept entered English for receiving and agreeing.
items.cn: accept 进入英语，表示接收与同意。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accept family; the near-meaning group is other verbs of agreeing.
note.cn: 形近组是 accept 词族；近义组是别的表示同意的动词。

definition_en: good enough to be allowed or agreed to, though not excellent
core_image: 一份试卷刚好压在及格线上，勉强过关
scene: 评审看了半天，最后说这份方案虽然不完美，但可以接受。The plan is not perfect, but it is acceptable.
sceneCN: 这里的 acceptable 指「可接受的」（第 1 个义项：达到可被接受的标准）；句意是这份方案不完美，但可以接受。

pos.zh: 可接受的；合格的；尚可的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -able 构成，义为「接受」

senses.title: Good enough to be accepted
senses.definition: meets the standard needed to be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 达到被接受所需的标准
senses.example: The plan is not perfect, but it is acceptable.
senses.exampleCN: 这份方案不完美，但可以接受。
senses.why: The -able ending means able to be, so acceptable is what can be accepted.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 意为「能被……的」，acceptable 就是能被接受的东西。

senses.title: Allowed by rules
senses.definition: allowed by a rule, custom or authority
senses.definitionCN: 被规则、习俗或权威所允许
senses.example: Such behaviour is acceptable in this office.
senses.exampleCN: 这种行为在这间办公室里是允许的。
senses.why: What a group will take in as proper is acceptable in the social sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体愿意当作合宜之事收下的，就是社会意义上的「可接受」。

senses.title: Tolerable but not good
senses.definition: barely good enough, though far from ideal
senses.definitionCN: 勉强够好，但远谈不上理想
senses.example: The food was acceptable, nothing more.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜还过得去，仅此而已。
senses.why: The word often carries a cool tone: taken, but not praised.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常带一点冷淡：收下了，但并不称赞。

definition_en: the act of receiving something, approving of it, or bearing it
core_image: 一双手从对面接过一份文件，随即在末尾签下名字
scene: 招聘会上，她接过录用通知，在签名栏写下自己的名字。Her acceptance of the offer came within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里的 acceptance 指「接受」（第 1 个义项：同意接收别人给出的东西）；句意是她在一分钟内就接受了这份工作。

pos.zh: 接受；认可；容忍；（票据）承兑

senses.title: Receiving what is offered
senses.definition: the act of agreeing to take something that is offered
senses.definitionCN: 同意收下别人递来的东西
senses.example: Her acceptance of the offer came within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一分钟内就接受了这份工作。
senses.why: The Latin verb accipere is built from ad-, towards, and capere, to take, so the noun first names the taking of something held out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 accipere 由 ad-（朝向）与 capere（拿取）组成，所以这个名词最初就指「把递到面前的东西收下」。

senses.title: Approval by others
senses.definition: the state of being approved of or believed by a group
senses.definitionCN: 被一群人认同或相信的状态
senses.example: The theory slowly gained acceptance among physicists.
senses.exampleCN: 这一理论逐渐获得物理学界的认可。
senses.why: Once a person takes an idea in, the idea is treated as his own; that inner taking became public approval.
senses.whyCN: 人把一种说法收进心里之后就会把它当成自己的，这种「收进来」就发展成了公开的认可。

senses.title: Bearing a hard situation
senses.definition: willingness to bear a difficult situation that cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 愿意承受无法改变的困难处境
senses.example: His calm acceptance of the loss impressed everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静地接受损失，让所有人都很佩服。
senses.why: A loss cannot be handed back, yet people still take it in, and that reluctant taking is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 损失退不回去，人却仍旧把它收进生活里，这份不情愿的收下就是「容忍」这一义项。

senses.title: Agreeing to pay a bill
senses.definition: a bank's formal promise to pay a bill of exchange
senses.definitionCN: 银行对汇票作出的正式付款承诺
senses.example: The bank's acceptance of the draft made the deal possible.
senses.exampleCN: 银行承兑了这张汇票，交易才得以完成。
senses.why: In trade the bank receives the draft and promises to honour it, which is the commercial branch of taking something in.
senses.whyCN: 在贸易中银行收下汇票并承诺付款，正是「收下」这个动作在商业里的专门用法。

intro.en: The word is a noun of taking, formed from a Latin verb that joined towards with to seize.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「拿取」的名词，来自一个由「朝向」与「抓住」拼成的拉丁动词。

items.cn: capere 意为拿取、抓住。

items.en: accipere added ad-, towards, and meant to receive.
items.cn: accipere 加上 ad-（朝向），意为接收。

items.en: acceptare stressed the repeated or willing side of receiving.
items.cn: acceptare 强调接收中反复、乐意的成分。

items.en: acceptance named the act of receiving favourably.
items.cn: acceptance 指欣然接收的行为。

items.en: the word entered English with both the personal and the legal sense.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时，既带个人层面的含义，也带法律层面的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accept family; the near-meaning group names approval and endurance.
note.cn: 形近组是 accept 词族；近义组表示认可与承受。

definition_en: the right or way to reach a place, person or set of data
core_image: 一扇门被刷卡打开，门后是一条直达深处的走廊
scene: 山脚下只有一座窄桥通向村子，外来车辆都得从那里过。The only access to the village is a narrow bridge.
sceneCN: 这里的 access 指「通道」（第 2 个义项：进入某地的路径）；句意是通往村子的唯一通道是一座窄桥。

义为「就职；加入；新增藏品」

senses.title: The right to enter
senses.definition: the right or opportunity to enter a place or use something
senses.definitionCN: 进入某个场所或使用某物的权利与机会
senses.example: Students have free access to the library.
senses.exampleCN: 学生可以免费使用图书馆。
senses.why: The Latin verb accedere means to go near, and a person who may go near a place holds this right.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 accedere 意为走近，被允许走近某个场所的人，手里的就是这项权利。

senses.title: A way in
senses.definition: a path or opening by which a place can be reached
senses.definitionCN: 通向某处的路径或开口
senses.example: The only access to the village is a narrow bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 通往村子的唯一通道是一座窄桥。
senses.why: If going near is the act, the route that makes the going possible is named by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然「走近」是动作，让这个动作得以发生的路线自然也用同一个词来命名。

senses.title: A chance to obtain
senses.definition: the opportunity to see, use or obtain information or people
senses.definitionCN: 看到、使用或取得信息与人员的机会
senses.example: Journalists had little access to the minister.
senses.exampleCN: 记者很少有机会接触这位部长。
senses.why: Information and powerful people are guarded like buildings, so reaching them is spoken of as gaining entry.
senses.whyCN: 信息与要人像建筑一样有人把守，所以接近他们也被说成「获得进入」。

senses.title: To open stored data
senses.definition: to reach and read files or records held by a computer
senses.definitionCN: 调取并读取计算机中保存的文件或记录
senses.example: You can access your files from any device.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以在任何设备上访问自己的文件。
senses.why: A file sits behind a password as a room sits behind a door, so the verb keeps the image of entering.
senses.whyCN: 文件躲在密码后面，就像房间在门后，所以动词仍保留「进去」的画面。

definition_en: an unfortunate event that happens by chance, or chance itself
core_image: 雨夜里两辆车在路口撞在一起，碎片散落一地
scene: 雨夜的路口，两辆车同时抢行，保险杠撞在一起。The accident blocked the road for two hours.
sceneCN: 这里的 accident 指「事故」（第 1 个义项：造成伤害或损坏的意外事件）；句意是这起事故让道路堵了两个小时。

senses.title: An unlucky event
senses.definition: an unfortunate event that causes injury or damage
senses.definitionCN: 造成伤害或损坏的不幸事件
senses.example: The accident blocked the road for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这起事故让道路堵了两个小时。
senses.why: The Latin verb accidere means to fall upon someone, and a sudden mishap is pictured as something falling on the victim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 accidere 意为「落到某人身上」，突如其来的祸事正被想象成落在受害者头上的东西。

senses.title: Chance without plan
senses.definition: the working of chance rather than intention
senses.definitionCN: 出于机缘而非有意安排
senses.example: I found the old photograph by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 我偶然找到了那张旧照片。
senses.why: What falls on a person without warning is not chosen by him, so the same noun came to name pure chance.
senses.whyCN: 毫无预警落到人身上的事不由人挑选，于是同一个名词也用来指纯粹的偶然。

senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由 accident 加 -al 构成，描述的正是像祸事那样不请自来、并非安排好的事。

senses.title: Not essential
senses.definition: belonging to something only by circumstance, not by its nature
senses.definitionCN: 仅因处境而附着，而非出于事物本性
senses.example: The colour is an accidental property of the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色是这种金属的附带属性。
senses.why: In philosophy an accident was a quality that could be removed while the thing remained itself, and the adjective kept that technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 在哲学里，accident 指去掉之后事物仍是自身的性质，形容词便保留了这一专门含义。

intro.en: The adjective is the noun accident with a Latin adjective ending attached.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是名词 accident 接上拉丁形容词词尾构成的。

items.en: accidere meant to fall upon or happen.
items.cn: accidere 意为降临、发生。

items.en: accidentalis described what was not part of a thing's essence.
items.cn: accidentalis 描述不属于事物本质的部分。

items.en: accidentel carried the philosophical sense into French.
items.cn: accidentel 把这个哲学含义带进法语。

items.en: accidental first meant non-essential in learned writing.
items.cn: accidental 最初在学术写作里指「非本质的」。

items.en: everyday speech shifted it towards unplanned events.
items.cn: 日常口语把它推向「未计划的事件」这一含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accident family; the near-meaning group names what happens without intent.
note.cn: 形近组是 accident 词族；近义组表示「非有意发生」。

entries.definition: happening as a minor part of something else

normalIntro.en: These hints follow the accident family, whose root means falling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条顺着 accident 词族走，它们的词根意为「落下」。

normal.en: accidental is accident turned into an adjective by -al.
normal.cn: accidental 就是 accident 加上 -al 变成的形容词。

normal.en: what falls on a person unasked is accidental.
normal.cn: 不请自来落到人身上的事，就是意外的。

normal.en: an accidental discovery is a finding nobody set out to make.
normal.cn: 意外的发现，是没人打算找到却找到的东西。

normal.en: in philosophy an accidental quality can be removed and the thing remains.
normal.cn: 哲学里，附带性质去掉之后，事物仍是它自己。

normal.en: the adverb accidentally says the act was done without meaning to.
normal.cn: 副词 accidentally 说明这个动作并非有意为之。

abstract.en: Picture a sleeve brushing a bottle and a crystal forming.
abstract.cn: 想象衣袖拂过瓶口，晶体悄然析出。

abstract.en: See two people turn a corner and meet without arranging it.
abstract.cn: 想象两人转过街角，毫无约定地遇见。

abstract.en: Think of a coat that can be taken off while the body stays.
abstract.cn: 想象外套脱下之后，身体依然如故。

examples.en: The accidental discovery changed the project.
examples.cn: 这项意外发现改变了整个项目。

examples.en: The fire was accidental, not set on purpose.
examples.cn: 这场火是意外，不是故意放的。

examples.en: Colour is an accidental feature of this mineral.
examples.cn: 颜色是这种矿物的附带特征。

dict_mnemonic.text: accident（意外）+ -al（……的）——带着「意外」性质的，就是 accidental。

root: 拉丁语 accidentalis（非本质的；偶发的），由 accidere（降临）加 -al 构成，本义「偶然附着的」，引申为意外与非本质。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective describes both what nobody planned and what a thing can lose and still remain itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词既描述没人计划过的事，也描述事物失去之后仍不改变本性的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sleeve knocking over a bottle and a surprise crystal.
core.cn: 核心意象：衣袖碰倒瓶子，意外得到晶体。

branches.en: a finding made while looking for something else
branches.cn: 找别的东西时得到的结果

branches.en: damage done without anyone intending it
branches.cn: 无人有意造成的损坏

branches.en: a colour that can change while the metal stays the same
branches.cn: 会变而金属本身不变的颜色

branches.en: a detail added by circumstance rather than by nature
branches.cn: 由处境而非本性添加的细节

branches.en: what is unplanned often turns out to be inessential
branches.cn: 未计划之物，往往也是非本质之物

definition_en: by mistake, or by chance rather than by plan
core_image: 手指一滑，刚整理好的文件从屏幕上消失
scene: 她一边回消息一边操作，手指一滑，把刚整理好的表格删掉了。She accidentally deleted the file she had just finished.
sceneCN: 这里的 accidentally 指「无意中」（第 1 个义项：因失误做了本不打算做的事）；句意是她不小心删掉了刚做完的文件。

senses.title: By mistake
senses.definition: does something by mistake that was never intended
senses.definitionCN: 因一时失误做了本来不打算做的事
senses.example: She accidentally deleted the file she had just finished.
senses.exampleCN: 她不小心删掉了刚做完的文件。
senses.why: The ending -ly turns accidental into a word about how an act is done, and the first use is the small slip that damages something.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把 accidental 变成描述「动作怎么做」的副词，最先用于那种手一滑就弄坏东西的失误。

senses.title: By chance
senses.definition: happens through luck or circumstance with no arrangement made
senses.definitionCN: 出于机缘巧合而发生，没有任何预先安排
senses.example: They accidentally met again in a Paris bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在巴黎的一家书店里偶然重逢。
senses.why: Not every unplanned act is a mistake; two people can meet without either doing wrong, so the same adverb also marks pure coincidence.
senses.whyCN: 并非每一件没计划的事都是失误，两个人相遇谁也没做错，于是同一个副词也用来标记纯粹的巧合。

intro.en: The adverb is the adjective accidental with an ending that says how something is done.
intro.cn: 这个副词是形容词 accidental 加上表示「以何种方式」的词尾。

items.en: cadere meant to fall.
items.cn: cadere 意为落下。

items.en: accidere meant to fall upon or happen.
items.cn: accidere 意为降临、发生。

items.en: accidentalis described what was not essential.
items.cn: accidentalis 描述非本质的部分。

items.en: accidental entered English as a word for unplanned qualities.
items.cn: accidental 进入英语，指非计划、非本质的性质。

items.en: -ly formed the adverb used for slips and coincidences alike.
items.cn: 加 -ly 之后形成的副词，同时用于失手与巧合。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accident family; the near-meaning group names unintended and chance action.
note.cn: 形近组是 accident 词族；近义组表示「非故意」与「碰巧」。

entries.definition: without being aware of what one is doing

normalIntro.en: These hints follow the accident family and its root meaning falling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条顺着 accident 词族和它「落下」的词根。

normal.en: accidental is the adjective; -ly tells you how the act was done.
normal.cn: accidental 是形容词，加 -ly 说明动作是怎么做的。

normal.en: the deleted file is the clearest picture of doing something accidentally.
normal.cn: 被删掉的文件，是「无意中做了某事」最清楚的画面。

normal.en: meeting an old friend accidentally carries no blame at all.
normal.cn: 偶然遇见旧友，这里面一点过错都没有。

normal.en: the root cadere, to fall, gives the sense of something dropping in unasked.
normal.cn: 词根 cadere 是落下，带来「不请自来掉下来」的感觉。

normal.en: keep the two uses apart: one is a slip, the other is luck.
normal.cn: 把两种用法分开：一种是失手，一种是运气。

abstract.en: Picture a finger sliding and a file vanishing.
abstract.cn: 想象手指一滑，文件消失。

abstract.en: See two old classmates turn into the same street at once.
abstract.cn: 想象两位老同学同时拐进同一条街。

abstract.en: Think of a coin landing on its edge by pure luck.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币纯凭运气立在了桌面上。

examples.en: She accidentally deleted the file she had just finished.
examples.cn: 她不小心删掉了刚做完的文件。

examples.en: They accidentally met again in a Paris bookshop.
examples.cn: 他们在巴黎的一家书店里偶然重逢。

examples.en: He accidentally knocked the cup off the table.
examples.cn: 他失手把杯子碰下了桌子。

dict_mnemonic.text: accidental（意外的）+ -ly（地）——以「意外」的方式做事，就是 accidentally。

root: 由 accidental 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；accidental 源自拉丁语 accidentalis，词根 cadere（落下），本义「以偶然、非计划的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb covers the slip of the hand and the luck of the meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词，既管手上的失手，也管相遇的运气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger slipping and a file disappearing.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指一滑，文件消失。

branches.en: a file deleted with no wish to delete it
branches.cn: 并不想删却删掉的文件

branches.en: a cup knocked over by a passing sleeve
branches.cn: 被衣袖带倒的杯子

branches.en: two people meeting with no appointment
branches.cn: 没有约定却相遇的两个人

branches.en: a discovery made while looking elsewhere
branches.cn: 在别处寻找时的发现

branches.en: both uses share the absence of intent
branches.cn: 两种用法共有的是「没有意图」

intro.en: The word is a Latin root, an adjective ending and an adverb ending stacked together.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁词根、形容词词尾与副词词尾层层叠加而成。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere, to fall, also gives cadence and decay.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cadere（落下）还给出 cadence 与 decay。

definition_en: a place to stay, an arrangement between sides, or the act of adjusting
core_image: 酒店前台递来一张房卡，行李箱终于有了落脚的地方
scene: 会议期间，主办方把代表们安排在海边的酒店住下。Hotel accommodation was included in the price.
sceneCN: 这里的 accommodation 指「住处」（第 1 个义项：供人居住的房间或场所）；句意是酒店住宿已包含在费用里。

derivatives.zh: 义为「容纳；为……提供住处；迁就」
义为「乐于助人的；随和的」

senses.title: A place to stay
senses.definition: a room, building or set of rooms where someone can live or sleep
senses.definitionCN: 供人居住或过夜的房间、建筑或成套房间
senses.example: Hotel accommodation was included in the price.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店住宿已包含在费用里。
senses.why: The Latin verb accommodare means to fit something to a need, and a room fitted to a traveller's need is the first thing the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 accommodare 意为「使适合某个需要」，为旅人需要而配好的房间，正是这个名词最先指的东西。

senses.title: A working agreement
senses.definition: an arrangement in which opposing sides accept a compromise
senses.definitionCN: 对立双方各自让步后达成的安排
senses.example: The two sides reached an accommodation over the border.
senses.exampleCN: 双方就边界问题达成了和解。
senses.why: When two claims must fit together, each side bends a little, so the idea of fitting became a word for settlement.
senses.whyCN: 两种主张要放到一起，双方都得弯一弯，于是「使相合」这个意思变成了「和解」。

senses.title: Adjustment to fit
senses.definition: the process of changing to suit new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 为适合新情况而作出改变的过程
senses.example: Accommodation to the high altitude took several days.
senses.exampleCN: 适应高海拔花了好几天。
senses.why: The core meaning is making one thing fit another, and the body or the eye doing that fitting is this abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意思始终是「让一物适配另一物」，身体或眼睛完成这种适配，就是这一抽象义项。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning to make something fit.
intro.cn: 这个词来自一个意为「使适合」的拉丁动词。

items.en: modus meant measure or proper size.
items.cn: modus 意为尺度、合适的大小。

items.en: accommodare meant to fit one thing to another.
items.cn: accommodare 意为使一物适配另一物。

items.en: accommodatio named the act of fitting or adjusting.
items.cn: accommodatio 指使适合、调节的动作。

items.en: accommodation carried the sense of lodging and of settling a difference.
items.cn: accommodation 在法语里兼指住宿与调解分歧。

items.en: the word now covers rooms, agreements and bodily adjustment.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖房间、协议与身体调节。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accommodate family; the near-meaning group names lodging and settlement.
note.cn: 形近组是 accommodate 词族；近义组表示住宿与和解。

entries.definition: to provide room for or adapt to
a place to sleep for a time
a deal in which both sides give something up
a small change made to suit conditions

normalIntro.en: These hints follow modus, the Latin word for measure.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语里表示「尺度」的 modus。

normal.en: accommodare is to fit one thing to another's measure.
normal.cn: accommodare 就是让一物合上另一物的尺寸。

normal.en: a hotel room is fitted to a guest, hence accommodation.
normal.cn: 酒店房间是按客人的需要配好的，所以叫 accommodation。

normal.en: two sides who each bend a little produce an accommodation.
normal.cn: 双方各让一步，就产生了 accommodation。

normal.en: the body fitting itself to thin air is accommodation to altitude.
normal.cn: 身体去适应稀薄空气，就是对高海拔的适应。

normal.en: the same idea of fitting runs through rooms, deals and lungs.
normal.cn: 「相合」这个意思贯穿房间、协议与肺。

abstract.en: Picture a key sliding into a lock that was made for it.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙滑进为它打造的锁孔。

abstract.en: See two negotiators pushing a table a little towards each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两位谈判者把桌子朝对方各推一点。

abstract.en: Think of a traveller setting a bag down in a small room.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人把行李放进一间小房间。

examples.en: Hotel accommodation was included in the price.
examples.cn: 酒店住宿已包含在费用里。

examples.en: The two sides reached an accommodation over the border.
examples.cn: 双方就边界问题达成了和解。

examples.en: Accommodation to the high altitude took several days.
examples.cn: 适应高海拔花了好几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（朝向）+ commod（合适的尺度）+ -ation——把东西调到合适的尺寸，就是「适配」，住处正是为住客配好的空间。

root: 拉丁语 accommodatio（适配），来自 accommodare：ad-（朝向）+ modus（尺度），本义「使合尺度」，引申为住处、和解与生理适应。

sensesIntro.en: One noun of fitting gives us a room fitted to a guest, a deal fitted to two sides, and a body fitted to thin air.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示「使相合」的名词，给出为客人配好的房间、为双方配好的协议，以及适应稀薄空气的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key settling into a lock made for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙落进为它打造的锁孔。

branches.en: a bed and a room prepared for a traveller
branches.cn: 为旅人备好的床与房间

branches.en: two claims trimmed until they fit together
branches.cn: 两种主张各削一点后拼合

branches.en: a body slowly fitting itself to thin air
branches.cn: 身体慢慢合上稀薄的空气

branches.en: both are a space or a body made ready for new conditions
branches.cn: 都是让空间或身体为新条件做好准备

branches.en: settling and adjusting both require giving a little
branches.cn: 和解与适应都需要让出一点

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a root for measure, a verb ending and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁前缀、表示尺度的词根、动词词尾与名词词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: The root modus, measure, also gives modify, mode and moderate.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 modus（尺度）还给出 modify、mode 与 moderate。

definition_en: to go somewhere with someone, to play music for them, or to happen at the same time
core_image: 舞台一侧的钢琴前，他为唱完最后一句的歌手轻轻收尾
scene: 演出最后一首曲子时，他坐在钢琴前为她伴奏。He accompanied her on the piano for the final song.
sceneCN: 这里的 accompany 指「为……伴奏」（第 2 个义项：用乐器为演唱者或独奏者配乐）；句意是最后一首歌由他用钢琴为她伴奏。

senses.title: To go with someone
senses.definition: to travel or go somewhere together with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人一起行走或前往某处
senses.example: Her brother accompanied her to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥陪她去了车站。
senses.why: The Old French compaign meant a companion, so the verb first describes being the person at another's side on the road.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 compaign 意为同伴，所以这个动词最初描述的是在路上站在别人身旁的那个人。

senses.title: To play for a singer
senses.definition: to play music that supports a singer or solo player
senses.definitionCN: 演奏音乐以支持演唱者或独奏者
senses.example: He accompanied her on the piano for the final song.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一首歌由他用钢琴为她伴奏。
senses.why: A pianist walks through the piece beside the singer, note for note, so the idea of going along moved into music.
senses.whyCN: 钢琴家一个音一个音地陪着歌手走完整首曲子，「同行」的意思于是进入了音乐。

senses.title: To happen together
senses.definition: to exist or occur at the same time as something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物同时存在或发生
senses.example: Thunder usually accompanies lightning.
senses.exampleCN: 雷声通常伴随着闪电。
senses.why: Two things that always arrive together behave like two travellers on one road, which gives this abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 总是同时出现的事物，就像同一条路上的两位旅人，这一抽象义项由此而来。

intro.en: The word goes back to a Latin phrase meaning with bread, used for someone who shares a meal.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到意为「同吃面包」的拉丁短语，用来指一起吃饭的人。

items.en: panis meant bread.
items.cn: panis 意为面包。

items.en: companio meant one who shares bread with another.
items.cn: companio 指与别人共享面包的人。

items.en: compaign meant a companion or mate.
items.cn: compaign 意为同伴、伙伴。

items.en: accompanien meant to be a companion on the way.
items.cn: accompanien 意为在路上做伴。

items.en: the verb grew senses of musical backing and of things happening together.
items.cn: 这个动词后来长出「伴奏」与「同时发生」两个义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accompany family; the near-meaning group names going along with someone.
note.cn: 形近组是 accompany 词族；近义组表示与人同行。

entries.definition: music or food that goes with something else
a person who plays for a singer
to go with someone to protect or guide them
to go with someone as a helper
to join someone as a companion
to happen at the same time

normalIntro.en: These hints follow panis, the Latin word for bread, and the companion who shares it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语里表示「面包」的 panis，以及分面包的伙伴。

normal.en: a companion is one who shares bread, and to accompany is to be that companion.
normal.cn: companion 是分面包的人，accompany 就是做那个分面包的同伴。

normal.en: the verb is spelled with two c's in the middle, like its Latin source.
normal.cn: 这个词中间有两个 c，跟着拉丁词源走。

normal.en: on the road the companion walks beside you; on stage the pianist plays beside you.
normal.cn: 路上同伴走在你旁边，台上钢琴家弹在你旁边。

normal.en: thunder accompanies lightning because the two never travel alone.
normal.cn: 雷伴随闪电，因为这两样从不单独出行。

normal.en: the passive form be accompanied by names whatever comes along.
normal.cn: 被动形式 be accompanied by 用来点出随行的那一样东西。

abstract.en: Picture two people sharing a loaf on a long walk.
abstract.cn: 想象两人在长途跋涉中分一只面包。

abstract.en: See a pianist leaning slightly towards a singer.
abstract.cn: 想象钢琴家微微侧向歌手。

abstract.en: Think of a flash and the rumble that always follows it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光与总跟着它的闷雷。

examples.en: He accompanied her on the piano for the final song.
examples.cn: 最后一首歌由他用钢琴为她伴奏。

examples.en: Her brother accompanied her to the station.
examples.cn: 她哥哥陪她去了车站。

examples.en: Thunder usually accompanies lightning.
examples.cn: 雷声通常伴随着闪电。

dict_mnemonic.text: com-（共同）+ pan（面包）——分同一块面包的人就是同伴，陪着你走、陪着你唱，都是 accompany。

root: 古法语 acompaignier（做伴），源自晚期拉丁语 companio：com-（共同）+ panis（面包），本义「共享面包的人」，引申为陪同、伴奏与伴随。

definition_en: to finish a task, or to bring about a result through effort
core_image: 最后一盏测试灯由红转绿，整块看板亮起完成
scene: 团队连续加班三周，终于把整套系统交付上线。They accomplished the task two days early.
sceneCN: 这里的 accomplish 指「完成」（第 2 个义项：把承担的事情做到完结）；句意是他们提前两天完成了任务。

derivatives.zh: 义为「技艺高超的；有造诣的」

senses.title: To produce a result
senses.definition: brings about a result by effort
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力带来某种结果
senses.example: She accomplished a great deal in her first year.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第一年就取得了很大成绩。
senses.why: The Old French verb acomplir meant to fill up completely, and a result is what fills the space that effort was aimed at.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 acomplir 意为「完全填满」，而努力的成果正是把原先瞄准的那块空白填满。

senses.title: To finish a task
senses.definition: brings a piece of work to its end
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作做到终点
senses.example: They accomplished the task two days early.
senses.exampleCN: 他们提前两天完成了任务。
senses.why: Something filled up is also something finished, so the same verb names the closing of a task.
senses.whyCN: 被填满的东西也是被做完的东西，于是同一个动词也用来指任务的收尾。

intro.en: The word comes from a French verb meaning to complete or fill up.
intro.cn: 这个词来自一个意为「完成、填满」的法语动词。

items.en: complere meant to fill up completely.

items.en: ad- added the idea of bringing something towards its end.

items.en: acomplir meant to carry something through to the end.
items.cn: acomplir 意为把某事做到底。

items.en: accomplish entered English as a verb of finishing work.
items.cn: accomplish 进入英语时，是表示「做完工作」的动词。

items.en: the word widened to cover achievements and skills.
items.cn: 后来它的范围扩大到成就与技艺。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accomplish family; the near-meaning group names finishing and achieving.
note.cn: 形近组是 accomplish 词族；近义组表示完成与达成。

definition_en: a formal agreement, harmony between things, or to grant and match
core_image: 两份文件末尾并排签下两个名字，随即交换文本
scene: 会议结束前，双方在文件末尾签字，握手合影。The two countries signed a peace accord that afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里的 accord 指「协议」（第 2 个义项：双方正式达成的约定）；句意是两国当天下午签署了和平协议。

senses.title: Harmony between things
senses.definition: a state in which two things agree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个事物彼此符合的状态
senses.example: His actions are in accord with his words.
senses.exampleCN: 他的行动与言语一致。
senses.why: The Latin phrase ad cor means to the heart, and two things brought heart to heart are in agreement.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad cor 意为「到心口」，两样东西被贴到心口相对，就是彼此相合。

senses.title: A formal agreement
senses.definition: an official arrangement accepted by two or more sides
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方正式接受的约定
senses.example: The two countries signed a peace accord that afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 两国当天下午签署了和平协议。
senses.why: When two sides bring their wishes heart to heart until they match, the written result is an accord.
senses.whyCN: 双方把各自的意愿摆到一起直到吻合，写下来的结果就是一份协议。

senses.title: To grant something
senses.definition: gives someone a right, honour or welcome
senses.definitionCN: 把某种权利、礼遇或欢迎给予某人
senses.example: They accorded her a warm welcome.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给予她热烈欢迎。
senses.why: What is granted is given in a spirit of agreement, so the verb of harmony also means to bestow.
senses.whyCN: 被授予的东西是在彼此合意中给出的，所以这个表示和谐的动词也用来指「给予」。

senses.title: To match or fit
senses.definition: matches or is consistent with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相吻合、不相抵触
senses.example: The results accord with our earlier theory.
senses.exampleCN: 结果与我们早先的理论相符。
senses.why: The verb simply performs the harmony the noun names, describing two things that fit without conflict.
senses.whyCN: 动词所做的，正是名词所指的那种和谐：两样东西彼此吻合、并不冲突。

intro.en: The word goes back to a Latin phrase meaning to the heart, used for bringing things into harmony.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到意为「到心口」的拉丁短语，用来表示把事物调和到一起。

items.en: cor meant heart.
items.cn: cor 意为心。

items.en: ad cor meant to the heart, and accordare meant to bring into harmony.

items.en: acorder meant to agree or reconcile.
items.cn: acorder 意为同意、和解。

items.cn: accord 既指和谐，也指写下来的和解。

items.en: the verb kept the sense of granting as well as matching.
items.cn: 动词则保留了「给予」与「相符」两层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accord family; the near-meaning group names agreement and granting.
note.cn: 形近组是 accord 词族；近义组表示一致与给予。

entries.definition: agreement with a rule or wish
in a way that suits what has happened
to give a right or favour

normal.en: facts that accord with a theory sit beside it without friction.

normal.en: of one's own accord means the heart moved first, with no push from outside.
normal.cn: of one's own accord 意为心先动了，外面没人推。

definition_en: agreement with a rule, wish or fact, chiefly in the phrase in accordance with
core_image: 施工图纸旁边摊着安全规范，两条线被逐条对齐
scene: 施工队进场前，先把图纸摊开，逐条对照当地的安全规范。All work was carried out in accordance with safety rules.
sceneCN: 这里的 accordance 指「依照」（第 2 个义项：以某项规定为行动依据）；句意是所有工作都依照安全规程进行。

pos.zh: 一致；依照（常用于 in accordance with）

senses.title: Agreement in state
senses.definition: the state of agreeing with something or being consistent with it
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物相合、并不抵触的状态
senses.example: There is no accordance between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 这两份报告之间并不一致。
senses.why: The noun is accord plus -ance, naming the state rather than the act, so it describes two things resting in agreement.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 accord 加 -ance，指一种状态而不是动作，描述的是两样东西彼此相合地摆在一起。

senses.title: Acting by a rule
senses.definition: the relation of acting exactly as a rule or wish requires
senses.definitionCN: 完全按照某项规则或意愿行事的关系
senses.example: All work was carried out in accordance with safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有工作都依照安全规程进行。
senses.why: In the fixed phrase in accordance with, the state of matching becomes the basis of action, so the word is read as according to.
senses.whyCN: 在固定短语 in accordance with 里，「相合」的状态成了行动的依据，于是这个词被理解为「按照」。

intro.en: The word is accord with a noun ending that turns agreement into a state.
intro.cn: 这个词是 accord 加上把「一致」变成状态的名词词尾。

items.en: the word now lives mainly inside in accordance with.
items.cn: 如今这个词主要活在 in accordance with 这个短语里。

entries.definition: in a way that follows from something
the act of obeying a rule
the state of matching or consenting

definition_en: as a result, or in a way that matches the situation
core_image: 暴雨预警亮起，运动会的日期在公告栏上被划掉改写
scene: 暴雨预警发布后，学校把原定的运动会改到下周。The schedule was changed accordingly.
sceneCN: 这里的 accordingly 指「相应地」（第 2 个义项：按照新的情况作出对应调整）；句意是日程也相应改了。

senses.title: As a consequence
senses.definition: introduces a result that follows from what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 引出由前文所述自然产生的结果
senses.example: The road was flooded, and accordingly the match was called off.
senses.exampleCN: 道路被淹，比赛因此取消。
senses.why: The word grew out of according, meaning matching; a result that matches its cause follows from it, and that following is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由意为「相合」的 according 长出，与原因相合的结果自然随之而来，这层「随之」就是此义项。

senses.title: In a matching way
senses.definition: in the way that the new situation requires
senses.definitionCN: 按照变化后的情况作出对应的调整
senses.example: The schedule was changed accordingly.
senses.exampleCN: 日程也相应改了。
senses.why: When the action must fit the circumstance rather than follow from it, the same adverb means doing things to match.
senses.whyCN: 当动作是要去迎合情况、而不是由情况推出时，同一个副词就表示「照着调整」。

intro.en: The adverb is according with an ending that turns it into a word about manner.
intro.cn: 这个副词是 according 加上表示方式的词尾。

items.cn: accordingly 形成，表示以相合的方式去做。

items.en: the word also took on the plain sense of therefore.
items.cn: 后来它又承担了「因此」这一直接含义。

entries.definition: as stated by someone or something

normalIntro.en: These hints follow according, whose older root means heart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条顺着 according，它的深层词根意为「心」。

normal.en: accordingly is according plus -ly, so it says how something is done.
normal.cn: accordingly 是 according 加 -ly，说明事情怎么去做。

normal.en: a cause and its result are two things that match, hence the sense therefore.
normal.cn: 原因和结果是彼此相合的两样东西，所以它有「因此」的意思。

normal.en: when the weather changes, the plan changes accordingly.
normal.cn: 天气变了，计划就相应地改。

normal.en: the word never stands alone at the front of a clause like a bare conjunction.
normal.cn: 这个词不像纯连词那样单独领起一个分句。

normal.en: act accordingly means let the action fit what you have just heard.
normal.cn: act accordingly 意为让行动合上你刚听到的情况。

abstract.en: Picture a date on a notice board being crossed out and rewritten.
abstract.cn: 想象公告栏上的日期被划掉重写。

definition_en: a record of money, a spoken or written report, a bill, or to explain and make up a share

scene: 他登录手机银行，看到工资已经到账。She checked her account before paying the rent.
sceneCN: 这里的 account 指「账户」（第 1 个义项：银行记录资金往来的户头）；句意是她在交房租前先查了账户。

senses.title: A record of money
senses.definition: an arrangement with a bank or service that records money paid in and out
senses.definitionCN: 与银行或服务机构之间记录资金进出的户头
senses.example: She checked her account before paying the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她在交房租前先查了账户。
senses.why: The Old French acont meant a reckoning of money, and the ledger where sums are counted became the modern bank account.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 acont 意为算账，数钱用的那本账，后来就变成了今天的银行账户。

senses.title: A report in words
senses.definition: a spoken or written description of an event
senses.definitionCN: 对某件事的口头或书面描述
senses.example: She gave a clear account of what happened.
senses.exampleCN: 她清楚地叙述了发生的事情。
senses.why: To give an account is to count out events one by one, so the money sense widened into telling a story.
senses.whyCN: give an account 原是把事件一件件数清楚，于是记账的意思扩展成了把事情讲出来。

senses.title: A bill owed
senses.definition: a statement of money owed for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 因货物或服务而欠款的清单
senses.example: Put the meal on my account, please.
senses.exampleCN: 这顿饭请记在我的账上。
senses.why: A record of what is owed is the oldest commercial use of the word, and it still names the bill itself.
senses.whyCN: 记录欠款是这个词最古老的商业用法，至今仍用来指账单本身。

senses.title: To explain
senses.definition: explains how or why something happened
senses.definitionCN: 说明某事如何发生或为何发生
senses.example: How do you account for the missing money?
senses.exampleCN: 你如何解释这笔不见了的钱？
senses.why: Giving an account of a matter is answering for it, so the verb account for means to explain.
senses.whyCN: 为一件事件给出交代就是为它作答，所以动词 account for 表示解释。

senses.title: To make up a share
senses.definition: forms a particular part of a total amount
senses.definitionCN: 构成总量中的某个部分
senses.example: Women account for half of the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 女性占员工总数的一半。
senses.why: When sums are counted, each group is entered as a share of the total, which is the numerical branch of accounting.
senses.whyCN: 算总账时每一类都要记成总数中的一份，这就是 account 在数字上的分支用法。

definition_en: the duty to explain one's actions and accept responsibility for them
core_image: 听证席上，一叠预算文件被推到发言人面前
scene: 听证会上，官员被要求逐项说明预算的去向。Voters demanded greater accountability from the council.
sceneCN: 这里的 accountability 指「问责」（第 1 个义项：必须对行为作出交代并接受监督）；句意是选民要求市政会接受更严格的问责。

senses.title: Being answerable to others
senses.definition: the state of being required to explain decisions to a public or an authority
senses.definitionCN: 必须向公众或上级说明决定的状态
senses.example: Voters demanded greater accountability from the council.
senses.exampleCN: 选民要求市政会接受更严格的问责。
senses.why: The noun is built on accountable, whose root is the counting of money; being made to count out one's decisions is the institutional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建立在 accountable 之上，词根是数钱记账；被要求把自己的决定一笔笔交代清楚，就是制度层面的问责。

senses.title: Taking responsibility oneself

senses.example: She showed real accountability for the mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个错误表现出真正的担当。
senses.why: The same duty can be worn from inside rather than imposed from outside, and that inner readiness is this second sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一份责任可以由外强加，也可以由内承担，这种主动承担就是第二个义项。

definition_en: a person who keeps or checks financial records, or in older use one who renders an account
core_image: 月底的办公室里，一摞票据被逐张核对后盖章
scene: 月底结账时，他把一摞票据交给会计核对。The accountant checked every receipt before closing the books.
sceneCN: 这里的 accountant 指「会计」（第 1 个义项：专业从事账务记录与核查的人）；句意是结账前会计核对了每一张票据。

senses.title: A keeper of financial records
senses.definition: a person whose job is to keep, check or advise on financial records
senses.definitionCN: 以编制、核查财务记录或就此提供意见为职业的人
senses.example: The accountant checked every receipt before closing the books.
senses.exampleCN: 结账前会计核对了每一张票据。
senses.why: The ending -ant marks a person, so from the verb of reckoning comes the one who does the reckoning for a living.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ant 标记做某事的人，于是从「算账」这个动作里走出了一个以算账为业的人。

senses.title: One who renders an account
senses.definition: in older use, a person who answers for money or goods entrusted to him
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指为所托付的钱款或货物作出交代的人
senses.example: The steward was the accountant of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 那名管事是这份产业的报账人。
senses.why: Before the word meant a profession, it simply named anyone obliged to report what he had received and spent.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词成为职业名称之前，它只是指任何一个必须报告自己收了多少、花了多少的人。
